- If sentiment is consistently negative over recent days, model tends to overcorrect downward; adjust forecast upward slightly to avoid excessive sell-off bias.
- If model shows sharp upward spike followed by forecast overshoot, reduce peak values by 5–10% to account for volatility overreaction.
- When sentiment is mixed or neutral, model often overestimates mean reversion; apply slight upward bias to reflect lingering momentum.
- If true outcome consistently lags model by 1–3 days, model may be overreacting to short-term sentiment; delay peak forecast by 1–2 days if sentiment is bearish.
- If model forecast mean is significantly higher than true outcome mean (especially in 30d horizon), reduce forecast by 2–5% to reflect underestimation of downward pressure.
- If sentiment shows strong bullish momentum but model forecasts remain flat or declining, increase forecast slope slightly to match sentiment trend.
- If sentiment is negative but true price is rising, model may be ignoring sentiment; adjust forecast to reflect sentiment’s influence on price direction.
